title: Scatter Graphs and Correlation
seo_title: Year 9 Scatter Graphs Worksheets: Correlation, Lines of Best Fit and Outliers
standard_text: Use and interpret scatter graphs of bivariate data; recognise correlation.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 scatter graph worksheets: describe positive, negative and no correlation, use a line of best fit to estimate, find outliers, and correlation vs causation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Positive: both go up. Negative: one goes up, the other goes down.
key_sub: Use a line of best fit only to estimate inside the data.
body_html:
How it works

A scatter graph plots pairs of values to show if two variables are linked. Positive correlation: as one goes up, the other goes up. Negative correlation: as one goes up, the other goes down. No correlation: no pattern. Points close to a line show strong correlation; spread-out points show weak correlation.

A line of best fit follows the trend. Use it to estimate values inside the data (interpolation). Estimates outside the data (extrapolation) are less reliable. Correlation does not prove that one thing causes the other.

Example

Revision hours and test scores rise together.

As one rises, so does the other.

Answer: Positive correlation

Example

Estimate a score for 4 hours.

Go up from 4 to the line, then across.

Answer: Read the value on the y-axis

Example

A point far from the others.

It does not fit the pattern.

Answer: An outlier

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up positive and negative correlation.
  • Saying 'no correlation' when the correlation is weak.
  • Reading the wrong axis when using the line of best fit.
  • Saying that correlation proves one thing causes another.

faq.a: A graph that plots pairs of values as points to show whether two variables are related.

faq.q: What are the types of correlation?
faq.a: Positive (both increase), negative (one increases while the other decreases) and none. Correlation can also be strong or weak.

faq.q: How do I draw a line of best fit?
faq.a: Draw a straight line that follows the trend, with roughly the same number of points on each side. It does not have to go through the origin.
No. Two things can be linked because a third thing affects both, such as hot weather increasing both ice cream sales and sunburn.

items.q: A line of best fit should…
c: Go through the first and last points
Follow the trend, with about the same number of points on each side
items.e: A line of best fit shows the trend. It does not have to go through any particular point: about the same number of points on each side.

items.q: When is it reliable to use a line of best fit to estimate?
c: When the value is far outside the data
Only when there is no correlation
When the value is inside the range of the data
items.e: Estimating inside the data (interpolation) is reliable. When the value is inside the range of the data.

items.q: Ice cream sales and sunburn cases show positive correlation. Does eating ice cream cause sunburn?
c: No, both are caused by hot sunny weather
No, because the correlation is negative
items.e: Correlation does not prove cause. Both are caused by hot sunny weather.

items.q: What does strong negative correlation mean?
c: As one increases, the other increases
As one variable increases, the other decreases, and the points are close to a line
items.e: As one variable increases, the other decreases, and the points are close to a line.

items.q: What is an outlier?
c: The point on the line of best fit
A value that does not fit the pattern of the rest
items.e: A value that does not fit the pattern of the rest. It may be a mistake or an unusual case.

items.q: Which pair of variables would most likely show no correlation?
c: The last digit of a phone number and running speed
Age and value of a phone
items.e: There is no reason for these to be linked: the last digit of a phone number and running speed.

items.q: A scatter graph of hours worked and pay shows strong positive correlation. Which statement is correct?
c: People who work more hours tend to earn more
People who work more hours earn less
Pay does not depend on hours
items.e: Positive correlation: people who work more hours tend to earn more.

items.q: What is the name for estimating a value inside the range of the data?
items.e: Inside the data is interpolation. Outside is extrapolation.

items.q: What is the name for estimating a value outside the range of the data?
items.e: Outside the data is extrapolation, which can be unreliable.

items.q: A graph of age and value of cars has a line of best fit. Why can't it be used for a 40-year-old classic car?
c: Classic cars may go up in value, and 40 years is outside the data
The line goes through the origin
Classic cars are outliers so the line is wrong
items.e: 40 years is outside the data, and classic cars may behave differently.

items.q: A line of best fit goes through (2, 30) and (6, 50). What is its gradient?
A line of best fit has gradient −2 and goes through (0, 40). Estimate y when x = 5.
Which of these shows the weakest correlation?
c: Points close to a falling straight line
Points close to a rising straight line
Points widely spread with a slight upward trend
items.e: Weak correlation means the points are widely spread: points widely spread with a slight upward trend.

items.q: Grace says: 'There is negative correlation, so one variable causes the other to fall.' Why is she wrong?
items.e: A link in the data does not prove that one causes the other. Correlation does not prove causation.

items.q: Which graph type is used to look for a relationship between two numerical variables?
items.e: Plotting pairs of values as points: a scatter graph.

items.q: Why might an outlier be removed before drawing a line of best fit?
c: It may be a mistake and would pull the line away from the trend
Outliers are always the most important
items.e: It may be a mistake and would pull the line away from the trend. Only remove it if there is a good reason.

items.q: A survey finds that towns with more libraries have more crime. What is the most likely explanation?
c: Bigger towns have more of both
items.e: Both depend on population: bigger towns have more of both.

items.q: On a scatter graph, temperature is plotted against heating cost. What correlation would you expect?
items.e: Warmer weather means less heating: negative.

items.q: A line of best fit predicts a test score of 120% for 30 hours of revision. What does this show?
c: Extrapolating far beyond the data gives impossible answers
items.e: Scores cannot be over 100%. Extrapolating far beyond the data gives impossible answers.

items.q: Which is the best description of 'no correlation'?
c: There is no linear relationship between the variables
The points form a straight line
items.e: There is no linear relationship between the variables.
